content:
**Fixed lane planner: secret groups over/under-reported in duplicates and skipped**

**What**: Fixed two related bugs in `planLaneCommit()` (brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.mjs): C5 — a group whose C2 winner was secret-marked still counted toward `duplicates` (over-report); C6 — a secret-marked LOSER in an otherwise-clean group was silently dropped, reported nowhere in `skipped` (under-report).
**Why**: Root cause was ordering: `occurrences.set(file, ...)` (feeding `duplicates` via `summarizeDuplicates`) ran unconditionally for any group with >1 candidate, BEFORE the code checked `winner.secret` — so a secret-skipped winner's group still got counted as a duplicate. Separately, only `winner.secret` was ever checked at all; a non-winning group member's `.secret` flag was never consulted, so it vanished with no skip entry.
**Where**: brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.mjs (the per-group loop, ~line 156-190), brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.test.mjs (extended the existing secret-winner test with duplicates assertions; added a new secret-loser test).
**Learned**: Fix order matters here — push a `secret` skip for EVERY marked member of the sorted group first (winner or loser), THEN check `winner.secret` to decide whether to register `duplicates` occurrences and push to `files`. This keeps the object-db guarantee (a secret winner never falls through to the runner-up) while making both the report (`skipped`) and the accounting (`duplicates`) consistent with which bytes actually got collected.
